heading: EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
translated_text:
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

REGENT OF CENTRAL BANGKA

BANGKA BELITUNG ISLANDS PROVINCE

COPY

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF CENTRAL BANGKA REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Central Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Central Bangka Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in families, society and community culture where we live, including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
6. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
11. Regional cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, made in writing and giving rise to rights and obligations.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

Empowerment and Protection of Women is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection of victims.

heading_path: HUMAN RIGHTS AND FUNDAMENTAL HUMAN FREEDOMS

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 6

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.
2. Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
3. In order to improve the position, role and quality of women as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family life, society, nation and state, women must be empowered.
4. Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (3) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, order and equality in enjoying the results of development.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 7

1. Women have the right to receive special protection from matters that threaten their safety and/or health.
2. Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.
3. Special protection as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of health services related to:
a. menstruation;
b. pregnancy;
c. childbirth; and
d. breastfeeding.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Women victims of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. Women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment.
2. Equal opportunities as referred to in paragraph (1) are realized through the fulfillment of women's rights to receive equal treatment from employers.
3. Employers who employ female workers must provide protection in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
4. Protection that must be provided by employers to women as referred to in paragraph (3) will be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide protection to women so that they can realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.
2. Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. The Regional Government facilitates the formation of women's protection institutions.
2. The Regent establishes policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the Region.
3. Implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by forming, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.
4. Membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
5. Further provisions regarding the Formation of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 12
Article 13
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 14

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. active role in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/orc. complaints/reports.
4. The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

FUNDING

Article 15

1. Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection in the Region shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Central Bangka Regency.
2. In the event that the Region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection from the Government, it must be implemented in accordance with the laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING

Article 16

1. To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection in the Region.
3. Monitoring shall be conducted periodically starting from planning up to the policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection for the current year.
4. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
5. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
6. The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's empowerment and protection to the Governor.
7. The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

SANCTIONS

Article 17

Any person who intentionally commits violence against women shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 18

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered, with its placement in the Regional Gazette of Central Bangka Regency.
